Hi. We're dealing with an error currently going on with our getList function throwing a TypeError. The details about the error can be found below:

### Describe the bug
With `namingConvention: "graphql-default"`, the Hasura data provider's `getList` throws `TypeError: v.toUpperCase is not a function` when a sorter targets a relation field such as `category.title`.

Since nested sorting landed ([#5508](https://github.com/refinedev/refine/pull/5508)), `generateSorting` returns a nested object for a relation field: `{ category: { title: "asc" } }`. For `graphql-default`, `getList` then calls `upperCaseValues(camelizeKeys(generateSorting(sorters)))` (`packages/hasura/src/dataProvider/index.ts:164`), and `upperCaseValues` (`packages/hasura/src/utils/upperCaseValues.ts:5`) calls `.toUpperCase()` on every value, including the nested `{ title: "asc" }` object.

With `hasura-default` naming the same sorter works.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `const dp = dataProvider(client, { namingConvention: "graphql-default" })`
2. `await dp.getList({ resource: "posts", sorters: [{ field: "category.title", order: "asc" }] })`
3. It throws `TypeError: v.toUpperCase is not a function` and no request is sent.
In a UI, sorting a table column that comes from a relation gives a failed list request instead of sorted data.

As failing tests on `main` @ `2352eb5b` (new `packages/hasura/test/getList/nested-sort.spec.ts`, plus a nested case in `test/utils/upperCaseValues.spec.ts`):

```
× upperCaseValues > should convert string values inside nested objects to upper case
× getList sorting by a relation field > sends nested order by with graphql-default naming convention
TypeError: v.toUpperCase is not a function
Tests  2 failed | 74 passed (76)
```

### Expected behavior
`getList` sends `orderBy: { category: { title: "ASC" } }`, the same way it already sends `{ title: "ASC" }` for a top-level field.

### Packages

- @refinedev/hasura 7.0.1 (current `main`, [2352eb5](https://github.com/refinedev/refine/commit/2352eb5b6539e2f39ad9aef652279ad1dcf2c467))

### Additional Context
A fix with a regression test is ready: `upperCaseValues` recurses into nested objects and upper-cases only string leaves (4 lines, plus a `@refinedev/hasura` patch changeset). With the fix the hasura suite passes 160/160. The GraphQL client is stubbed in the test; no live Hasura server was used. I'd like to open the PR against this issue.

*Found and fixed by an AI agent (breken-ai), run against refine's own test suite.*

Please familiarize yourself with the area of this repository that relates to the issue and any other relevant areas, and please give me a summary of your understanding.

**Clarifying camelizeKeys**

I’m thinking about how camelizeKeys works, especially with nested keys. When I encounter a relation like `category.title`, it seems that it generates `category.title` without changing `category` since it’s likely already in camelCase. If I have a snake_case nested field, using camelizeKeys in a shallow manner wouldn’t touch those nested keys. I don’t want to overcomplicate things here, and I realize no additional tools are needed for this!

I traced the relevant Hasura flow:

- [`generateSorting.ts`](/home/jdperez/repos/refine_forked/packages/hasura/src/utils/generateSorting.ts) converts dotted fields such as `category.title` into nested objects:
  ```ts
  { category: { title: "asc" } }
  ```
- In [`dataProvider/index.ts`](/home/jdperez/repos/refine_forked/packages/hasura/src/dataProvider/index.ts), `hasura-default` uses that structure directly. `graphql-default` passes it through `camelizeKeys` and then [`upperCaseValues.ts`](/home/jdperez/repos/refine_forked/packages/hasura/src/utils/upperCaseValues.ts).
- `upperCaseValues` currently assumes every value is a string and calls `.toUpperCase()`. Nested relation sorters therefore cause the reported `TypeError`.
- The correct fix is for `upperCaseValues` to recurse through nested objects and uppercase only string leaves, preserving the nested Hasura order-by structure.
- The regression belongs both in the utility test and in a `getList` test asserting:
  ```ts
  orderBy: { category: { title: "ASC" } }
  ```
